text:
sam: FYI starting a config-only rollout now: cfg-2026-03-19a. Changes: per-request timeout 30s -> 18s, qps cap 600 -> 450, burst 1200 -> 900, batch_window_ms 8 -> 8 (initial), low-priority models routed to standby pool. Canary 5% us-west. change window 20m.

deploy-bot: rollout initiated: cfg-2026-03-19a -> service/inference (canary=5%) at 1954123456. Live links: https://console/redwood/deploys/1954123456

tess: noted, watching latency + cost dashboards :eyes:

kevin: what's the rollback criteria? pls spell it out so SRE knows thresholds.

sam: Rollback triggers: 1) 99p latency increase >50ms over baseline sustained >5m, 2) error-rate (5xx) jump >0.5 percentage points, 3) cache-hit ratio drop >6% relative. If any hit, auto-rollback to previous config.

anya: can we pin the routing-model policy to avoid model churn during test? last time we had a model switch mid-canary and it confounded things.

sam: good call. pinning routing policy to model_tag=prod-stable-20260312 for this rollout.

deploy-bot: routing policy pinned: model_tag=prod-stable-20260312 (route_pin_id=rp-20260319-01)

oncall-bot: created monitors for latency_99p, error_5xx_rate, kv_cache_hit. Alert targets: #oncall and sam,tess.

kevin: doing a quick smoke against canary endpoints now. curl looks good but measuring tail samples. snippet:

```
curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test tail"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST'
```

kevin: first 3 runs OK, latencies 120-160ms. will continue sampling.

(t + 6m) tess: small 99p uptick to +65ms vs baseline, sustained ~6m. error rate flat. cache-hit down 2%.

sam: seeing that too in the dashboard. that's beyond our latency trigger. hold ramp and investigate. do NOT increase canary pct.

anya: propose a soft rollback for the routing rewrite only (route low-priority back to main pool) while keeping timeout and qps caps. that should reduce tail.

kevin: agree. safe rollback for the route change only. how do we run that?

sam: I'll submit a config patch to revert routing rewrite and keep other params. patch id cfg-2026-03-19a-rev1. rolling that to canary now.

deploy-bot: patch rollout started: cfg-2026-03-19a-rev1 (routing revert) -> service/inference (canary still 5%) at 1954123472

(t + 3m) oncall-bot: monitor update: latency_99p back down to +18ms vs baseline, error rate unchanged, cache-hit recovered to +0.5%

sam: good. canary remains at 5% for the rest of the change window. next steps: 1) adjust batch_window_ms from 8 -> 12ms in next minor config to see if it smooths tails, 2) hold routing pin until end of day, 3) add a short A/B to test the timeout reduction impact on fail-open behavior.

tess: I'll update the release note and include the rollback decision and pinned routing policy.

sam: release note draft: "cfg-2026-03-19a — config-only change: reduced per-request timeout, lower QPS caps, initial canary paused after tail latency increase; routing-rewrite reverted in canary. routing pinned to prod-stable-20260312. follow-ups: tweak batching window and refine latency alert thresholds."

kevin: copying that into the deploy ticket. tagging oncall for post-mortem if regressions occur.

deploy-bot: rollout status: canary paused -> stable not promoted. change window still open until 1954124556.

sam: thanks everyone. keep watching dashboards for the next 40m, and report anything >1% error delta or latency >100ms above baseline.
